title: Osaka Execution Spec -- Fork Types
description: Core type definitions for Osaka fork: Account, Address, Root, VersionedHash, Bloom, Authorization, encode_account, and EMPTY_ACCOUNT.

sub_graphs.name: Primitive Type Aliases
sub_graphs.description: Defines fundamental Ethereum type aliases used throughout the Osaka fork specification. These aliases map domain-specific names to their underlying byte/hash representations.

invariants.text: Address is always a 20-byte value (Bytes20), corresponding to the length of an Ethereum address derived from the last 20 bytes of a Keccak-256 hash.
Root is always a 32-byte hash (Hash32), representing a Merkle-Patricia trie root.
VersionedHash is always a 32-byte hash (Hash32), used for EIP-4844 blob versioned hashes.
Bloom is always a 256-byte value (Bytes256), representing a 2048-bit Bloom filter for log indexing.

state_variables.name: Address
state_variables.description: Type alias for a 20-byte Ethereum address.

state_variables.name: Root
state_variables.description: Type alias for a 32-byte Merkle-Patricia trie root hash.

state_variables.name: VersionedHash
state_variables.description: Type alias for a 32-byte versioned hash used in EIP-4844 blob transactions.

state_variables.name: Bloom
state_variables.description: Type alias for a 256-byte (2048-bit) Bloom filter used for log event indexing.

sub_graphs.name: Account Data Structure
sub_graphs.description: Defines the Account dataclass representing the state associated with an Ethereum address. The Account is a frozen (immutable) slotted dataclass containing nonce, balance, and code fields. This is the core state representation for every account in the Ethereum state trie.

invariants.text: Account instances are immutable (frozen) once created, enforced by the @slotted_freezable and @dataclass decorators.
The nonce field must be an unsigned integer (Uint) representing the number of transactions sent from the account (for EOAs) or the number of contracts created (for contract accounts).
The balance field must be a 256-bit unsigned integer (U256) representing the account's balance in Wei.
The code field must be a byte sequence (Bytes) representing the account's EVM bytecode. For externally owned accounts (EOAs), this is empty.

data_structures.name: Account

fields.name: nonce
fields.description: Transaction count (EOA) or contract creation count. Prevents replay attacks and determines contract addresses.

fields.name: balance
fields.description: The account's Ether balance denominated in Wei (1 Ether = 10^18 Wei).

fields.name: code
fields.description: EVM bytecode associated with the account. Empty bytes for externally owned accounts.

sub_graphs.name: Empty Account Sentinel
sub_graphs.description: Defines the EMPTY_ACCOUNT constant, a canonical representation of an account with zero nonce, zero balance, and empty code. This sentinel value is used for comparisons to determine whether an account is 'empty' per EIP-161, which affects state pruning and gas cost calculations.

invariants.text: EMPTY_ACCOUNT.nonce is always Uint(0).
EMPTY_ACCOUNT.balance is always U256(0).
EMPTY_ACCOUNT.code is always empty bytes (b"").
EMPTY_ACCOUNT is a frozen Account instance and cannot be modified after creation.

state_variables.name: EMPTY_ACCOUNT
state_variables.description: Canonical empty account instance used as a sentinel for EIP-161 empty account checks and state pruning.

sub_graphs.name: Account RLP Encoding
sub_graphs.description: Defines the encode_account function that serializes an Account dataclass into its RLP-encoded representation for storage in the Ethereum state trie. Notably, storage is not part of the Account dataclass and must be provided separately as a storage root hash. The encoding follows the account state format: [nonce, balance, storage_root, code_hash].

invariants.text: The RLP encoding always produces a tuple of exactly four elements in order: (nonce, balance, storage_root, keccak256(code)).
The account code is never stored directly; it is always hashed with Keccak-256 before encoding.
Storage root must be provided externally since it is not part of the Account dataclass. This reflects the separation of account state from account storage in Ethereum's state model.

functions.name: encode_account
functions.signature: def encode_account(raw_account_data: Account, storage_root: Bytes) -> Bytes
functions.description: Encode Account dataclass. Storage is not stored in the Account dataclass, so Accounts cannot be encoded without providing a storage root.

parameters.name: raw_account_data
parameters.description: The Account dataclass instance containing nonce, balance, and code.

parameters.name: storage_root
parameters.description: The Merkle-Patricia trie root hash of the account's storage, provided separately from the Account dataclass.

functions.return_description: RLP-encoded bytes of the tuple (nonce, balance, storage_root, keccak256(code)).

preconditions.text: raw_account_data must be a valid Account instance with nonce (Uint), balance (U256), and code (Bytes) fields.
storage_root must be a valid Bytes value representing the Merkle root of the account's storage trie.

postconditions.text: Given the same Account and storage_root inputs, encode_account always produces the same RLP-encoded output (deterministic encoding).
The returned Bytes can be decoded via RLP to recover the original tuple (nonce, balance, storage_root, code_hash).

state_transitions.description: encode_account is a pure function with no side effects. It does not modify any state; it only transforms input data into an RLP-encoded byte representation.

sub_graphs.name: Authorization Data Structure (EIP-7702)
sub_graphs.description: Defines the Authorization dataclass used in set-code transactions (EIP-7702). An Authorization represents a signed delegation that allows an EOA to temporarily set its code to a specified contract address. It contains chain_id for replay protection, the target address, a nonce, and an ECDSA signature (y_parity, r, s).

invariants.text: Authorization instances are immutable (frozen) once created, enforced by the @slotted_freezable and @dataclass decorators.
The chain_id field is a U256, providing chain-specific replay protection for the authorization.
The address field is an Address (Bytes20), specifying the target contract whose code will be delegated to.
The nonce field is a U64, preventing replay of the same authorization.
The signature is split into three components: y_parity (U8, recovery bit), r (U256), and s (U256), forming a valid ECDSA signature.

data_structures.name: Authorization
data_structures.description: The authorization for a set code transaction (EIP-7702).

fields.name: chain_id
fields.description: The chain ID for replay protection. Must match the current chain to be valid.

fields.name: address
fields.description: The target contract address whose code the EOA delegates to.

fields.name: nonce
fields.description: Authorization nonce preventing replay of the same delegation.

title: Osaka Execution Spec -- Requests
description: EIP-7685 request framework. Defines deposit, withdrawal, and consolidation request types. Implements extract_deposit_data, parse_deposit_requests, and compute_requests_hash (SHA2-256).

sub_graphs.name: EIP-7685 Request Type Constants and Contract Identifiers
sub_graphs.description: Defines the core constants for the EIP-7685 request framework: the three request type byte prefixes (deposit=0x00, withdrawal=0x01, consolidation=0x02), the deposit contract address, and the deposit event signature hash. These constants form the foundation for identifying and categorizing contract-triggered requests that are exposed to the consensus layer.

invariants.text: DEPOSIT_REQUEST_TYPE = b'\x00'. The deposit request type byte is always 0x00.
WITHDRAWAL_REQUEST_TYPE = b'\x01'. The withdrawal request type byte is always 0x01.
CONSOLIDATION_REQUEST_TYPE = b'\x02'. The consolidation request type byte is always 0x02.
DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS = 0x00000000219ab540356cbb839cbe05303d7705fa. This is the canonical Ethereum deposit contract address and must not change.
DEPOSIT_EVENT_SIGNATURE_HASH = 0x649bbc62d0e31342afea4e5cd82d4049e7e1ee912fc0889aa790803be39038c5. This is the keccak256 hash of the DepositEvent signature and is used to filter deposit logs.

state_variables.name: DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS
state_variables.description: The canonical Ethereum 2.0 deposit contract address.

state_variables.name: DEPOSIT_EVENT_SIGNATURE_HASH
state_variables.description: The keccak256 hash of the deposit event signature.

state_variables.name: DEPOSIT_REQUEST_TYPE
state_variables.description: Single-byte type prefix for deposit requests.

state_variables.name: WITHDRAWAL_REQUEST_TYPE
state_variables.description: Single-byte type prefix for withdrawal requests.

state_variables.name: CONSOLIDATION_REQUEST_TYPE
state_variables.description: Single-byte type prefix for consolidation requests.

security_notes: The deposit contract address is hardcoded and immutable. Any change would constitute a consensus-breaking modification.
Request type bytes must be unique and non-overlapping.
The deposit event signature hash must exactly match the keccak256 of the DepositEvent ABI signature.

sub_graphs.name: Deposit Event ABI Encoding Layout
sub_graphs.description: Defines the fixed ABI encoding layout for deposit events emitted by the deposit contract. Specifies exact byte offsets and sizes for the five deposit data fields: pubkey (48 bytes at offset 160), withdrawal_credentials (32 bytes at offset 256), amount (8 bytes at offset 320), signature (96 bytes at offset 384), and index (8 bytes at offset 512). The total deposit event data length is exactly 576 bytes.

invariants.text: DEPOSIT_EVENT_LENGTH = 576. Every valid deposit event data blob must be exactly 576 bytes in length.
The ABI layout uses fixed offsets: PUBKEY_OFFSET=160, WITHDRAWAL_CREDENTIALS_OFFSET=256, AMOUNT_OFFSET=320, SIGNATURE_OFFSET=384, INDEX_OFFSET=512.
The field sizes are fixed: PUBKEY_SIZE=48, WITHDRAWAL_CREDENTIALS_SIZE=32, AMOUNT_SIZE=8, SIGNATURE_SIZE=96, INDEX_SIZE=8. Total extracted = 192 bytes.
The encoded offset values in the first 160 bytes must exactly match the expected constant offsets. Any deviation causes an InvalidBlock exception.
The encoded size values at each field's offset position must exactly match the expected constant sizes. Any deviation causes an InvalidBlock exception.

state_variables.name: DEPOSIT_EVENT_LENGTH
state_variables.description: The exact byte length of a valid deposit event data blob.

state_variables.name: PUBKEY_OFFSET
state_variables.description: Byte offset where the pubkey field begins.

state_variables.name: WITHDRAWAL_CREDENTIALS_OFFSET
state_variables.description: Byte offset where the withdrawal_credentials field begins.

state_variables.name: AMOUNT_OFFSET
state_variables.description: Byte offset where the amount field begins.

state_variables.name: SIGNATURE_OFFSET

state_variables.name: INDEX_OFFSET

state_variables.description: Size in bytes of the validator public key (BLS12-381 compressed).

state_variables.name: WITHDRAWAL_CREDENTIALS_SIZE
state_variables.description: Size in bytes of the withdrawal credentials hash.

state_variables.name: AMOUNT_SIZE
state_variables.description: Size in bytes of the deposit amount (little-endian uint64, in Gwei).

state_variables.name: SIGNATURE_SIZE
state_variables.description: Size in bytes of the BLS12-381 signature.

state_variables.name: INDEX_SIZE
state_variables.description: Size in bytes of the deposit index (little-endian uint64).

data_structures.name: DepositEventLayout
data_structures.description: The ABI-encoded deposit event data layout. The first 160 bytes contain 5 big-endian uint256 offset values. At each offset, there is a 32-byte size prefix followed by the actual field data.

security_notes: Strict validation of all offsets and sizes provides defense-in-depth against malformed deposit event data.
Big-endian encoding of offsets requires careful byte-order handling.
The 576-byte length check is the first validation gate.

sub_graphs.name: Deposit Data Extraction and Validation (extract_deposit_data)
sub_graphs.description: Implements extract_deposit_data(data: Bytes) -> Bytes, which validates the ABI encoding structure before extracting five deposit fields and returning them as a concatenated 192-byte result. Any validation failure raises InvalidBlock.

invariants.text: Raises InvalidBlock if the input data length is not exactly 576 bytes.
Raises InvalidBlock if any of the 5 offset values do not match the expected constants (160, 256, 320, 384, 512).
Raises InvalidBlock if any of the 5 size values do not match the expected constants (48, 32, 8, 96, 8).
On success, returns exactly 192 bytes: pubkey(48) + withdrawal_credentials(32) + amount(8) + signature(96) + index(8).
The extraction order is deterministic and consensus-critical: pubkey, withdrawal_credentials, amount, signature, index.

functions.description: Validates ABI encoding structure of a deposit event data blob and extracts five deposit fields into a concatenated byte string. Performs 11 validation checks: 1 length, 5 offsets, 5 sizes.
functions.pseudo_logic: assert len(data) == 576; validate offsets; validate sizes; extract and concatenate fields; return 192 bytes

pre_conditions.text: Input 'data' must be a raw bytes object from a deposit contract log entry.
Caller has verified the log originates from DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS with matching event signature.

post_conditions.text: If successful, returned Bytes is exactly 192 bytes: pubkey(48) + withdrawal_credentials(32) + amount(8) + signature(96) + index(8).
If any validation fails, InvalidBlock is raised and no partial data is returned.

state_transitions.from_state: Raw ABI-encoded deposit event data (576 bytes)

security_notes: 11 independent validation checks provide defense-in-depth.
InvalidBlock is consensus-critical: malformed deposits invalidate the entire block.
Strict offset/size validation prevents out-of-bounds reads.
Concatenation order is consensus-critical.

sub_graphs.name: Block-Level Deposit Request Collection (parse_deposit_requests)
sub_graphs.description: Iterates through all transaction receipts in block execution output, scans logs for deposit events from the deposit contract, and aggregates extracted deposit data into a single concatenated byte string preserving receipt/log order.

invariants.text: Only logs from DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS with topics[0] == DEPOSIT_EVENT_SIGNATURE_HASH are processed.
Deposit requests are accumulated in receipt trie key order, then log index order.
Every receipt referenced by block_output.receipt_keys must exist in the receipts trie.
The returned byte string length is always a multiple of 192. Empty if no deposits found.

functions.description: Scans all transaction receipts for deposit events, extracts deposit data from matching logs, and returns concatenated deposit data.
functions.pseudo_logic: deposit_requests = b''; for key in receipt_keys: receipt = trie_get(); for log in decoded_receipt.logs: if deposit match: deposit_requests += extract_deposit_data(log.data); return deposit_requests

pre_conditions.text: block_output.receipt_keys must contain keys for all receipts in correct execution order.

post_conditions.text: Returned Bytes contains all deposit data, length = N * 192 where N = number of deposit events.
If any deposit event data is malformed, InvalidBlock propagates up.
If no deposit events found, returns b''.

state_transitions.trigger: Any deposit event data validation fails
Receipt key has no trie entry

security_notes: Dual-filter (address + event signature) prevents spoofed deposit events.
topics[0] check requires len(log.topics) > 0 first, preventing index-out-of-bounds.
Receipt ordering is consensus-critical.
Receipt decoding must handle all receipt types (legacy, EIP-2718 typed).

sub_graphs.name: Requests Hash Computation (compute_requests_hash)
sub_graphs.description: Computes a SHA2-256 commitment hash over a list of request byte strings using a double-hashing scheme. Each request is individually SHA256-hashed, then digests are fed into a final SHA256 accumulator. This hash is stored in the execution block header.

invariants.text: Uses SHA2-256 (not keccak256), imported from hashlib.sha256.
Hash = SHA256(SHA256(req[0]) || SHA256(req[1]) || ... || SHA256(req[n-1])), using incremental update.
Output is always exactly 32 bytes (256 bits).
Order of requests is significant. Different ordering produces different hash.
Empty list produces SHA256('') = e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855.

functions.description: Computes SHA2-256 hash commitment using double-hashing scheme. Returns 32-byte digest.
functions.pseudo_logic: m = sha256(); for req in requests: m.update(sha256(req).digest()); return m.digest()

pre_conditions.text: The requests list contains typed request byte strings (type prefix + data).
The requests list is ordered deterministically (by type, then extraction order).

post_conditions.text: The hash uniquely commits to both content and order of all requests.

state_transitions.from_state: Ordered list of request byte strings

security_notes: SHA2-256 (not keccak256) is used for cross-layer compatibility with the beacon chain.
Double-hashing provides Merkle-like commitment without full tree.
Order-dependence is consensus-critical.
Empty-list case must be handled correctly by all implementations.

sub_graphs.name: EIP-7685 Request Framework Architecture
sub_graphs.description: The overarching EIP-7685 request framework. Requests are a general-purpose mechanism for storing contract-triggered requests in the execution layer, extending both header and body. Supports three request types: deposits (0x00), withdrawals (0x01), consolidations (0x02).

invariants.text: EIP-7685 extends execution block header with requests_hash (32-byte SHA2-256) and block body with requests list.
Request types distinguished by single-byte prefix: 0x00=deposit, 0x01=withdrawal, 0x02=consolidation.
Block header requests_hash must equal compute_requests_hash output. Mismatch invalidates block.
All requests are deterministically extracted from block execution output, not user-submitted.

data_structures.name: BlockOutput
data_structures.description: Block execution output structure containing receipts trie and receipt keys for request extraction.

fields.name: receipt_keys
fields.value: Ordered list of trie keys for all receipts

state_transitions.to_state: Requests extracted and committed in header

state_transitions.trigger: Block header received by consensus layer

security_notes: SHA2-256 commitment creates trust bridge between execution and consensus layers.
Deterministic extraction ensures all honest nodes produce identical request lists.
Type-prefix system must maintain uniqueness when adding new request types.
Dependencies on decode_receipt, trie_get, BlockOutput must all be correct.
